findings.effect: A truncated turn skips the word cap entirely, even when notTruncated is not set to report a failure. A reply exceeding maxReplyWords can therefore pass when it hits the output cap.
findings.reason: Names assertions.ts at line 250 and quotes the seeded condition, explaining how truncated replies bypass maxReplyWords.

findings.effect: maxReplyWords silently skips the word check on truncated turns. A case without notTruncated can therefore pass the word check without reporting truncation.
findings.reason: Names assertions.ts and quotes the seeded condition, explaining that truncated turns can pass without a word-limit failure.

findings.effect: When a turn ends on the proposal card, the empty textAfterProposal value is omitted because it is falsy. The assertion falls back to the whole reply, including text before the tool call, and incorrectly fails the reply word limit despite there being no closing text.
findings.reason: Names driver.ts at line 325 and explains how dropping empty textAfterProposal causes pre-proposal text to count and falsely fail the limit.

findings.effect: When there is no text after the proposal, the empty string is dropped from the turn. maxReplyWords then falls back to the whole assistant reply and grades text written before the proposal.
